title: Smithfield budget review board sets 22-slide, 30-minute cap on department presentations
text:
← Back to the wire
Government
Smithfield budget review board sets 22-slide, 30-minute cap on department presentations
The board also decided presentations must summarize, not duplicate, any written report a department submits beforehand.
The Smithfield Financial Budget and Financial Review Board agreed Tuesday, Oct. 13, that department budget presentations will be limited to 22 slides and 30 minutes.
SLIDE RULES During the meeting, members worked through draft budget process guidelines section by section, including a slide presentation requirement. The draft language stated slide presentations "may not exceed 22 slides, may not exceed 30 minutes" and "must directly support budget."
Members debated the word "directly" in that requirement. One board member said, "I don't necessarily I I don't like making assumptions," leading the board to revise the language to specify that slides should be "summarizing, not duplicating" a report if one was provided.
REPORTS COME FIRST The board also agreed that any formal written report should be delivered before the presentation itself. A board member explained the reasoning, saying the presentation "is like like the language we use. It's an executive summary of a larger data set." Another member responded, "I like that Peter delivered prior to the presentation."
TIME CONSTRAINTS The guidelines also addressed what happens if a department needs more time. The board agreed to keep a bullet point stating that if time constraints exist, departments should contact the chair to request a specific allotment on the agenda, though members discussed formatting that provision as a separate, standalone item rather than grouping it with other bullets.
The discussion was part of a broader review of proposed fiscal year 2028 budget process guidelines, which the board did not formally adopt by vote during the meeting.
